Samira — thanks, this is great context. Below is a concise implementation playbook and a tiny Go sample you can drop into your infra. I also included the cutover checklist and rollback triggers we recommend.

High level playbook (summary)
- Week -2: Provision IP allowlist, SSO metadata exchange, and KMS access (if you will use customer-managed keys).
- Week -1: Integration sandbox testing with SDK samples + synthetic load (50k tokens/day emulation).
- Day 0: Start canary at 5% traffic to dedicated pool, monitor latency, error-rate, cost-per-token.
- Day 1: Increase to 25% if SLOs met. Day 2: Full cutover if stable. Rollback to hosted if error rate > 1% sustained for 15 minutes or 95th p50 latency degradation > 40%.

Client-side rate limit guidance
- Read rate headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset. Treat 429 as a soft stop: backoff and retry with jitter.
- Recommended client token budget: keep a 10% buffer below X-RateLimit-Limit to prevent races across distributed clients.
- Graceful degrade: fallback to shorter responses, lower sampling temperatures, or cached embeddings if remaining quota is low.

Timeouts / Retries (recommended)
- Per-request timeout: default 15s for chat/generation calls, 5s for quick embeddings (adjust to your latency distribution).
- Retry policy: retry idempotent calls up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff (base 200ms, factor 2) + full jitter. Do NOT retry on 4xx except 429.
- Streaming: detect partial stream failures and attempt a single recovery fetch for missing suffix tokens; do not restart long-running streams more than once.

Tiny Go SDK sample (drop-in):

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "net/http"
    "time"
)

func callGeneration(ctx context.Context, client *http.Client, apiKey, endpoint string, body []byte) (string, error) {
    // per-call timeout
    ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 15*time.Second)
    defer cancel()

    req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", endpoint+"/v1/generate", nil)
    req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+apiKey)
    // simple client header for rate limit visibility
    req.Header.Set("X-Client-Name", "novastack-integration")

    // basic retry with backoff and jitter (pseudo)
    var lastErr error
    backoff := 200 * time.Millisecond
    for attempt := 0; attempt < 3; attempt++ {
        resp, err := client.Do(req)
        if err == nil && (resp.StatusCode >= 200 && resp.StatusCode < 300) {
            // parse response body (omitted)
            // inspect rate limit headers
            // rl := resp.Header.Get("X-RateLimit-Remaining")
            return "<generated_payload>", nil
        }
        lastErr = err
        // handle 429 specially: increase backoff
        time.Sleep(backoff)
        backoff = backoff * 2
    }
    return "", fmt.Errorf("failed after retries: %v", lastErr)
}

// Note: this is an intentionally small sample. See attached sdk-samples-go-v1.zip for full helpers (retries, metrics, streaming).

Cutover checklist (MOP items)
- Confirm traffic toggle flag and canary percentage control in NovaStack router.
- Announce maintenance window to stakeholders and on-call.
- Provision allowlist + SAML metadata + KMS bindings.
- Enable prefix caching and KV cache warm-up for large models.
- Start canary (5%), monitor 1m/5m error spikes, token cost delta.
- If stable, move to 25% after 12 hours, then 100% after 48 hours.

Rollback triggers
- >1% errors for 15m or error spikes tied to authentication or 503s.
- X-RateLimit-Remaining falls below 5% for any major route.
